identity.title: VideoJAM: Joint Appearance-Motion Representations for Enhanced Motion Generation in Video Models

problem.claim: Generative video models struggle to capture real-world motion, dynamics, and physics.

gap.claim: The abstract attributes this limitation to pixel reconstruction objectives that favor appearance fidelity over motion coherence.

contributions.claim: VideoJAM jointly learns appearance and motion by predicting generated pixels and corresponding motion from one learned representation during training.
Inner-Guidance uses the model’s evolving motion prediction to steer inference toward coherent motion.
The framework is presented as broadly applicable to video models with minimal adaptations, without changing training data or model scale.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce VideoJAM as a framework combining joint appearance–motion representation learning with inference-time Inner-Guidance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art motion-coherence performance, surpassing highly competitive proprietary models.
The authors report improved perceived visual quality alongside improved motion coherence.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing generative video models are described as weak at realistic motion, dynamics, and physics.
The authors link the limitation to pixel reconstruction objectives that prioritize appearance over motion coherence.
VideoJAM combines joint pixel-and-motion prediction during training with Inner-Guidance during inference.
The authors report leading motion coherence, gains in perceived visual quality, and performance above proprietary competitors.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a stated failure mode—appearance-biased reconstruction—with two corresponding interventions: joint motion learning and motion-based inference guidance.

lessons.interpretation: A compact problem-to-mechanism mapping can make a method’s design rationale easier to evaluate.
lessons.application: When presenting a model, explicitly connect each component to the diagnosed objective or inference failure it is intended to address.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the method has multiple independent goals or when the failure diagnosis is not supported by the available evidence.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative metrics, datasets, evaluation protocol, or details of the proprietary-model comparisons.
The claimed broad applicability and minimal adaptation requirements are not operationally specified in the abstract.
